_meta.scope: Geologic subsurface CO2 sequestration capacity (supercritical CO2 in saline aquifers + depleted oil/gas fields). Excludes mineralization/basalt pathways except where noted as alt estimates.
known_access_failures: Kearns et al. 2017 (Energy Procedia 114:4697-4709, doi:10.1016/j.egypro.2017.03.1603) primary per-region table could NOT be extracted: ScienceDirect and ResearchGate both blocked with CAPTCHA/security-check pages across multiple fetch attempts (direct WebFetch and r.jina.ai proxy). Only the global 8,000-55,000 Gt headline figure and fragmentary secondary-cited regional numbers (North America 2,600-21,770 Gt; Asia ~2,964-2,984 Gt; South America ~2,030 Gt, via a 2025 CCUS-policy review citing Kearns) were recoverable. Treat the 'regions' array below as LOW CONFIDENCE / illustrative, not a faithful reproduction of Kearns Table 3.

global.notes: These three numbers are NOT a single confidence interval on one quantity -- they are anchors from three different, non-comparable methodological tiers, presented together because each is the most-cited figure in its tier: (1) low = 'prudent' risk-screened limit (Gidden et al., Nature 2025, central 1,460 Gt, range 1,290-2,710 Gt) after applying depth/seismic/protected-area/transboundary exclusion layers to a starting physical potential of ~11,800 Gt; (2) central = CSRC/OGCI Cycle 4/5 aggregated Stored+Commercial+Sub-Commercial+Undiscovered resource across ~54-111 assessed countries (~14,300 Gt), which -- reassuringly -- lands close to the low end of Kearns et al. 2017's independently-derived 8,000-55,000 Gt 'practically accessible' range; (3) high = Kearns et al. 2017 upper bound of practically accessible theoretical capacity worldwide. The spread illustrates that 'global CO2 storage capacity' answers differ by >1 order of magnitude depending on how aggressively non-technical risk/access constraints are applied, not because the underlying geology is disputed.
sources: OGCI CSRC Cycle 4 Main Report (Aug 2024) and Cycle 5 Main Report (Aug 2025), https://www.ogci.com

Gidden et al. (2025), 'A prudent planetary limit for geologic carbon storage', Nature 645:124-, doi:10.1038/s41586-025-09423-y, PMC12408384

countries.notes_research: CSRC's '0' reflected a genuine data gap at the time (Cycle 4, Aug 2024), closed by the IFC atlas published March 2025. 10,700 Gt is a prospective/theoretical-tier figure (analogous to CSRC 'Undiscovered'), not a mature resource number, and should be treated with the same caveats as other basin-scale prospective estimates -- but it is the best available and most recent national assessment. Flag for reconciliation once CSRC Cycle 6 potentially incorporates it. || 2026-10-15 verification: CSRC Cycle 4 Appendix F (p.13) shows 0.00 Gt in all classes with 'no published information'; Nigeria absent from CSRC Cycle 5 Table 4-3, so not updated in Cycle 5. IFC atlas Figure E2 (p.13) bars summed: low 2,742 / medium 10,757 (text: 10,700) / high 29,046 Gt at SE 0.5/2/5.4% (Goodman et al. 2011). Niger Delta Basin row (1,595/6,258/16,897) is the Niger Delta subset of the same figure. Depleted/near-depleted fields 3.4 Gt separate (section 6.9). Caveat: the atlas's Dahomey table (Table 6.3) repeats the Chad Bima/Gongila row inputs and volumes exactly (7,978 area, 62,000/241,000/651,000 Mt), and the Chad bar in Figure E2 (455/1,787/4,826) exceeds Table 6.4's two plays (89.7/349.7/944.5), so basin-level values inside the atlas are internally inconsistent; national total used as published.
